title: Once again, NASA is asking for ideas to rescue Hubble from certain death
gist: NASA has issued a Request For Information asking commercial firms how they would reboost Hubble to at least 600 km, service it or guide it to a controlled reentry, with a mission by 2032. Without intervention, Hubble is expected to reenter in 2033-2034. NASA has no funding allocated, but a maturing satellite-servicing industry (Northrop Grumman/DARPA, Astroscale, Starfish Space, Katalyst's Swift attempt) makes a robotic rescue more plausible than in 2022.

themes.theme: Hubble's decaying orbit and the RFI

insights.claim: Hubble has no onboard propulsion and has drifted down from 583 km in 2002 to about 470 km today. Without intervention it will likely reenter in 2033 or 2034, though forecasts shift with solar activity.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: There is a hard deadline of a few years for any commercial rescue.
insights.quote: Orbital dynamicists currently predict that it will likely happen in 2033 or 2034 without intervention

insights.claim: NASA's RFI asks for current and near-term capabilities to capture Hubble and boost it to at least 600 km, enhance its performance, or guide it to a controlled reentry. The mission must not harm the telescope, is expected by 2032, and responses are due November 30.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: This opens a near-term demand signal for in-space servicing companies.
